text: Sativasur is a town and municipality located in the Colombian Department of Boyacá, within the Northern Boyacá Province subregion. It is about 132 km from Tunja, the department's capital. The municipality shares borders with Sativanorte to the north, Socotá to the east, and Paz de Río to the south and west. Before the Spanish conquest of the Muisca in the central highlands (Altiplano Cundiboyacense) in 1540, both Sativasur and Sativanorte were known as Sátiva. This area was inhabited during the Herrera Period and was governed by the cacique of Tundama, now known as Duitama, which was part of the Muisca Confederation. The Spanish conquistadores who arrived in 1540 were Gonzalo Suárez Rendón and Hernán Pérez de Quesada. Sativasur was officially established on January 30, 1720. The names Sativasur and Sativanorte originate from the cacique Sátiva, whose name in the Chibcha language of the Muisca means "Captain of the Sun." The primary economic activities in the area are agriculture, livestock farming, and mining.
